passages.text: God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth, and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how. For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
passages.note: patience; growth happens slowly and unseen

passages.text: How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it? It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth, yet when it is sown, grows up, and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.
passages.note: small beginnings can grow into something great

passages.text: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
passages.note: unappreciated by family and those closest

passages.text: He said to them, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
passages.note: overwork and exhaustion; the need to rest
